evaluation_policy.detection_scope: only items not requiring patch context
evaluation_policy.detection_scope_note: ir_real_01/02/03 (2026-09-11): the buggy code alone IS self-evident (wrong pi/e/tau constants, an off-by-one contradicting the function's own docstring), but no category in the 8-value taxonomy honestly describes 'wrong hardcoded constant, no exception in real usage' -- assertion_violation would be dishonest (no assert in the real source, only in the harness) and incorrect_result is not a valid categories value. Kept in patch_context_items (excluded from the LLM detection-accuracy metric) for that reason, not because they need the patch to be understood. Still fully mined, patched, and ESBMC-confirmed via bugs/. 2026-09-28: 11 items whose bug is visible from the code alone returned to the detection metric (now scored by harness_strategies); the remaining ones need project-specific knowledge. Duplicates av_real_19, av_real_20, ip_real_31 and vm_real_09 were removed.

description: ESBMC-verifiable subset of bugs_reais (18 of 115 items). Built by scripts/build_v2_eligible.py from eligibility.json; do not edit by hand.

items.abstraction_notes: num_substrings = len(possible_substrings_splits[i]) can legitimately be 0 (an empty split option) -- nothing upstream of the real division guards against it. Manual assert added because ESBMC-Python's `/` is not covered by the default division-by-zero check. Verified: esbmc --z3 --unwind 6 --timeout 20s -> VERIFICATION FAILED.
items.eligibility_reason: Divisão real por num_substrings == 0; fix protege a divisão. invalid_precondition removida no elegível: não há evidência independente (o fix é um guard local, não validação de entrada).

items.abstraction_notes: A hashed cron field with a malformed/inverted range (e.g. "* * R/0 * *") makes range_end - range_begin + 1 == 0; nothing before the real `%` rejects that. Manual assert isolates the real ZeroDivisionError trigger (int `%` is not the checked `//`). Verified: esbmc --z3 --unwind 6 --timeout 20s -> VERIFICATION FAILED.
items.eligibility_reason: Módulo por zero real; o fix valida a faixa e lança CroniterBadCronError, o que é evidência independente de precondição de entrada.

items.abstraction_notes: dict.get() with no default returned None for status codes outside the known table, crashing downstream string formatting; fix adds an 'Unknown Status' default. Modeled as a bool precondition (was the status in the table), no scrapy-internal types needed.
items.eligibility_reason: TypeError real: dict.get sem default devolve None para to_native_str. invalid_precondition removida no elegível: mesma evidência da none_misuse.

items.expression: len(self._dict) == len(that) and all((self[key] == that[key] for key in self))
items.abstraction_notes: Real code indexed `that[key]` for every key in `self` without first checking `key in that`, raising KeyError when comparing against a dict missing one of self's keys. Reproduced near-verbatim with two literal dict values (self_d={a:1,b:2}, that_d={a:1}); ESBMC's dict subscript model raises the missing-key access as an array-bounds violation (CWE-125), the internal representation of the same real KeyError.
items.recommended_timeout: 60s (1740 VCCs, times out at the default 20s)

items.abstraction_notes: Inverted 'is None' where 'is not None' was intended, so make_current() raised RuntimeError exactly backwards (when there wasn't already a current loop instead of when there was). Modeled as a bool-inversion pair.
items.eligibility_reason: RuntimeError real lançado com condição invertida em entrada válida; fix inverte o teste.

items.abstraction_notes: The doubly-linked PamdRule list reduced to a single bool (next_is_none) standing in for 'current_line is the last node'; the real prev/next pointer rewiring is omitted since the bug is purely the missing None-guard on current_line.next before dereferencing .prev on it.
items.eligibility_reason: NULL dereference nativo ao acessar current_line.next.prev com next None; fix adiciona o guard.

items.abstraction_notes: Function builds a matches list, then only returns inside `if matches:` with no else -- when matches is empty, implicitly returns None instead of []. Real GitHub issue #18. Verified via ESBMC's missing-return-statement detection (120 VCCs generated, 26 after simplification).
items.eligibility_reason: Missing return nativo: caminho sem return devolve None; fix sempre retorna a lista.

items.abstraction_notes: Verbatim: indexes self._cached[0] unconditionally; real fix guards with `if self._cached:`. Reproduced directly with an empty list literal, no stubbing needed.
items.eligibility_reason: IndexError nativo na operação real; o patch do commit elimina a falha com a mesma main.

items.abstraction_notes: Verbatim: src_txt[-1] on an empty string raises IndexError; real fix uses the slice src_txt[-1:], which is safe on an empty string. Reproduced directly with an empty string literal, no stubbing needed.
items.eligibility_reason: IndexError nativo na operação real; o patch do commit elimina a falha com a mesma main.

items.abstraction_notes: Real code guarded l[i+4] with 'i+3 < len_l' instead of 'i+4 < len_l'; when len_l == i+4 exactly the guard passes but the index is out of range. Modeled as a plain int-indexed list, no dateutil token types needed.
items.eligibility_reason: IndexError nativo na operação real; o patch do commit elimina a falha com a mesma main.

items.abstraction_notes: end was set directly to the caller-supplied n without clamping to len(pwcs); when n exceeds the string length the loop indexes past the end. Fixes real issue #228, has an upstream regression test.

items.abstraction_notes: x[0] accessed unconditionally; natsort's own regex splitting can produce an empty string, which then IndexErrors here. Fix adds an 'if not x' guard. Issue-linked, has a regression test.
items.eligibility_reason: IndexError nativo na operação real; o patch do commit elimina a falha com a mesma main.

items.abstraction_notes: In the ZWJ branch, result[-1] and string[i-1] are accessed with no non-empty/i>0 guard; a string starting with a zero-width-joiner triggers IndexError on the first char. Real issue #263, has a regression test. Reproduced verbatim with the deterministic empty-result/i=0 trigger case.
items.eligibility_reason: IndexError nativo na operação real; o patch do commit elimina a falha com a mesma main.

items.abstraction_notes: lines[0] indexed with no empty-list check; raises IndexError when 'uname -rs' produces no output. Pure Sequence[str] function, no subprocess dependency at this level. Fixes real GitHub issue #304/#264.
items.eligibility_reason: IndexError nativo na operação real; o patch do commit elimina a falha com a mesma main.

items.abstraction_notes: Real code called configure_http_handler() on the metrics VALUE returned by generate_latest() instead of on the metrics_collector object that actually defines that method. Modeled with two minimal classes (Metrics with no such method, MetricsCollector with it) -- ESBMC-Python's class model raises AttributeError on the wrong-object call, near-verbatim reproduction.
items.eligibility_reason: AttributeError nativo: método chamado no objeto errado; fix chama no coletor.

items.abstraction_notes: Isolated the scalar step_size computation from an NKI hardware kernel (tensor/tile ops, out of ESBMC-Python's scope, left untouched in detection/). Real caller precondition (h_src > 0, chunk_size > 0, default chunk_size=10) preserved via __ESBMC_assume; no lower bound of 2 on chunk_size existed pre-fix, so chunk_size == 1 collapses step_size to 0. Manual assert added because ESBMC-Python's `/` lowers to ieee_div and is not covered by the default division-by-zero check. Issue #125 filed by Lucas Cordeiro (formal verification researcher), fixed by PR #126 (assert chunk_size >= 2). Verified: esbmc --z3 --unwind 6 --timeout 20s -> VERIFICATION FAILED, counterexample chunk_size=1.
items.eligibility_reason: Divisão por step_size == 0; o fix (PR #126) acrescenta assert chunk_size >= 2 na entrada, evidência independente de precondição.

items.abstraction_notes: A non-list-like serialized field value falls into `self._xg_characters(serialized_value)` unconditionally; _xg_characters calls `.decode(self.encoding)` on anything not already text, so an int/float field (no .decode method) raises AttributeError. Visible from the real code alone: _xg_characters's own body (shown right below the call site) does the isinstance check that decides whether .decode() runs. Modeled with a bool flag standing in for 'the field value is already text'.
items.eligibility_reason: AttributeError nativo: .decode() em valor int; fix converte com str().
